newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar's fall hammers U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar's fall hammers U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were depressed by the dollar's rapid fall against the yen by Tokyo midday on Thursday in thin activity, traders said.
"The Treasuries' falls reflect mainly the dollar's weakness this morning, but apart from that activity was very quiet, with many Japanese sidelined," a Japanese brokerage trader said.
Traders said underlying sentiment is still mixed, with speculation of credit-tightening in the U.S. still strong.
"Looking at the extent of the price gains overnight after the weaker-than-expected PPI data, the trend has not turned bullish yet," the trader said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was at 96-19/32, yielding 6.89 percent, against 96-23/32 in New York. June T-bond futures fell 2/32 from the previous close to 110-3/32.

Traders said light position adjustments dominated activity after overnight rises, with traders waiting for U.S. consumer price index and industrial production data later in the day to determine market trends.
Further deterioration of the dollar against the yen could accelerate the falls in Treasury prices, they said.
The dollar fell as low as 115.70 yen in Tokyo in the morning, against a 117.30/40 yen close in New York overnight.
